Clinical Features: New-onset hypertension after 20 weeks' gestation plus evidence of maternal endothelial dysfunction and/or uteroplacental dysfunction
Increased risk if single kidney (including transplant), autonomic neuropathy, polyhydramnios, multiple pregnancy, obstructed labor
Vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain, uterine tenderness
Vomiting, polydipsia, jaundice, elevated transaminases, hypoglycemia
Hemolysis and end organ damage including kidney failure, neurologic symptoms, heart disease
Tachycardia, fever, uterine tenderness, abnormal lochia, prolonged rupture of membranes
Operative delivery, fever, leucocytosis, pain, persistent ileus
Hyperkalemia, exacerbation of hypertension, fluid retention
Dysuria, back or flank pain, renal angle tenderness, hypotension
Proteinuria ± hematuria, malaise, joint pain, hair loss, rash, pancytopenia
uPCR >30 mg/mmol or uACR >8 mg/mmol before 20 weeks warrants nephrology referral
New drug exposure including antibiotics, NSAID, proton pump inhibitors, H₂ antagonists; systemic signs can include rash and fever
Renal colic; increased risk of AKI if single kidney
